title: Operator shift heuristics and interruption minimization playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook documents operator-first heuristics for shift handoffs and minimizing interruption cost on Redwood’s inference platform. It is intended for platform operators, SREs, and oncall engineers who steward runtime-proxy, batch-scheduler, kv-cache, prefetch-coordinator, and tenant-routing services during regional operations. The goal is to reduce cognitive load across shift boundaries, reduce interruption frequency, and accelerate safe resolution in ways that preserve latency and cost SLOs.

When to use this document

- During every 1st/2nd line shift handoff.
- When an incident originates from noisy alerts or repeated short interruptions.
- When preparing for maintenance windows or high-traffic events (Black Friday / major enterprise rollouts).

Key goals and metrics (what success looks like)

- Reduce median interruption duration per shift to < 8 minutes.
- Decrease number of interrupting alerts that require > 5 minute interaction by 30% quarter-over-quarter.
- Interruption Tax (new KPI): aggregate operator time spent per 10k tokens served. Target: <= 0.05 operator-minutes/10k tokens.
- Maintain platform SLOs during handoffs: p95 response latency < 180ms for foreground routes, token-error-rate < 0.05% across dedicated pools.

Ownership and roles

- Operator (current shift): primary action taker for alerts and oncall pagers.
- Handoff owner (incoming shift): responsible for absorbing ownership and validating preflight checks within 10 minutes of start.
- Runbook author (platform-team): maintains this doc and associated CLI helpers.
- Escalation engineer (eng-sre): invoked when an incident matches tier-2 escalation criteria (see Escalation matrix).

Pre-shift checklist (run by outgoing operator, 15 minutes before shift end)

1) Alerts snapshot
   - Open the platform-alerts dashboard (dash: /dashboards/platform/operator-shift-summary).
   - Note top 3 alert groups by frequency in last 4h.

2) Synthetic checks and warmers
   - Run: curl -sS https://runtime-proxy.internal/health | jq .status -> expect "ok".
   - Verify kv-cache hit rate > 78% for high-throughput tenants. Command: ./ops-cli metrics get kv_cache_hit_rate --window 60m.

3) Active rollouts and experiments
   - List canaries: ./ops-cli rollout list --active. Communicate any canary with >10% error drift to incoming.

4) Notable operator actions in last shift
   - Fill one-line summary in handoff channel: #operator-handoff with bullet list.

Handoff script (structured, 10 minutes)

1) Context transfer (3 minutes)
   - Outgoing: summarize recent incidents, ongoing rollouts, and muted alerts. Include the Interruption Tax and any operator time spent on each incident.
   - Incoming: confirm read and acknowledge three items aloud in the channel.

2) Validate preflight (3 minutes)
   - Incoming runs the same health checks described above. If any check fails, follow the Quick corrective actions below before final acceptance.

3) Acceptance and takeover (4 minutes)
   - Incoming posts takeover message with timestamp and the current token cost/p95 snapshot. Outgoing confirms release of active escalation duties.

Quick corrective actions (for preflight failures)

- runtime-proxy unhealthy:
  1) Check controller logs: kubectl -n runtime logs deploy/runtime-proxy -l app=runtime-proxy --tail=200
  2) If >30% pods are CrashLoopBackOff, scale temporarily: kubectl scale deploy/runtime-proxy --replicas=desired (use last-known-good replicas if available).
  3) If scaling fails, route traffic to regional fallback: ./ops-cli routing set-priority --region fallback-eu --policy degrade-latency.

- kv-cache hit rate drop:
  1) Inspect eviction spikes: ./ops-cli metrics get kv_cache_evictions --window 15m --group-by shard
  2) If a shard is hot, trigger shard-split: ./ops-cli cache shard-split --shard <id>
  3) If split not feasible within 20 minutes, enable targeted prefetch: ./ops-cli prefetch enable --tenant <id> --policy conservative

- High token-error-rate:
  1) Check model-variant fallback logs: ./ops-cli logs modelrouter --filter 'fallback' --since 30m
  2) If a model variant is failing, initiate emergency-model-swap: ./ops-cli model swap --from <variant> --to <stable-variant> --safe-checks true

Interruption minimization heuristics (principles)

- Reduce noisy alerts: favor aggregated symptoms over single-source metrics. Use alert suppression windows for transient degradations shorter than 90s.
- Favor operator-initiated experiments over ad-hoc fixes during handoff windows. If a change will take >10 minutes of operator time, schedule it in the maintenance cadence.
- Priority to preserve SLOs: If an action risks p95 spike by >20% for more than 5 minutes, prefer a graceful fallback (route to a lower-cost but stable variant) rather than live tuning.

Alert triage decision tree (short form)

1) Is the alert blackbox (external customer impact) or whitebox (internal metric)?
   - Blackbox -> escalate to customer-success and open incident bridge within 2 minutes.
   - Whitebox -> continue triage.
2) Is traffic degraded (p95 > 1.2x SLO) or is it isolated to a tenant?
   - Global degradation -> run global fallback matrix (see section below).
   - Isolated tenant -> apply tenant-slice soft-quota or targeted prefetch.
3) Can a one-line mitigation reduce operator involvement?
   - Yes -> apply mitigation and monitor 10 minutes.
   - No -> escalate per matrix.

Global fallback matrix (quick reference table)

- Symptom: Runtime CPU exhaustion
  Action: Shift noncritical tenants to spot-pool; enable reduced-batch-size.
  Command: ./ops-cli tenant relocate --policy spot-buypass --criteria noncritical

- Symptom: p95 latency degradation across regions
  Action: Increase cache TTLs for foreground routes, route traffic away from affected region.
  Command: ./ops-cli routing set-region-weight --region us-east-1 --weight 0.3

- Symptom: Model variant panic (OOM / kernel fault)
  Action: Swap to previous stable variant and throttle requests.
  Command: ./ops-cli model swap --to <stable-variant>; ./ops-cli throttle set --route /generate --rate 0.6

Operator tooling snippets (copyable)

- Health summary (one-liner):
  ./ops-cli health summary --region $REGION | tee /tmp/health-${REGION}.txt

- Inject synthetic request to validate end-to-end:
  curl -sS -X POST https://runtime-proxy.internal/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' -d '{"prompt":"health-check","max_tokens":8}' | jq .latency

- Quick rollback to last model:
  ./ops-cli model rollback --service runtime --confirm

Escalation matrix (who to call)

- Tier 1 (oncall operator): first 10 minutes.
- Tier 2 (eng-sre escalation): if unresolved after 10 minutes or if p95 > 2x SLO or token-error-rate > 1%. Contact: eng-sre-rotation@redwood.internal.
- Tier 3 (platform leads): if customer-impacting for > 30 minutes or repeated regression across regions. Page: +1 555-0241-ops.

Handoff channel templates (must be used verbatim)

- Outgoing summary template:
  SHIFT OUT -> TIME: ${TS}
  1) Top alerts: [name] x N in 4h
  2) Active rollouts: [model-a canary: 12% error drift]
  3) Actions in-flight: [cache-split on shard 12]
  4) Interruption Tax (last 8h): 17 operator-minutes / 100k tokens

- Incoming acceptance template:
  SHIFT IN -> TIME: ${TS}
  ACK: I have run preflight checks and accept ownership. Key snapshot: p95=${P95}, token-cost=${TOKEN_COST}/1k, active-canaries=${CANARIES}

Retention and post-shift notes (5 minutes at end of incoming's first hour)

- Incoming must append 1–3 bullet notes summarizing any changed state or new mitigations. Keep them short and actionable so the outgoing of the next shift can read them in < 2 minutes.

Change gating around handoffs (policy)

- No change that requires >5 minutes operator time is allowed within the 10-minute handoff window unless it's emergency-labeled.
- Any model-variant rollout that increases traffic by >10% must have a rollback plan and an owner who will be oncall for 60 minutes post-rollout.

Training, drills, and retrospectives

- Quarterly operator drills: simulate 6 interruption events in a 2-hour lab to practice quick handoffs. Use the synthetic-scenario-orchestrator (playbook id: lab-operator-008).
- After-action note template: list root-cause, what minimized operator time, what increased interruption tax, and a 30-day action (owner + ETA).

Appendix A — Example handoff transcript (redacted)

- Outgoing: "Top alert: runtime-proxy p95 spike 210ms after kernel swap at 14:02. Active canary: model-v2b (20% traffic). I split shard 12 at 14:37 — hit rate recovered to 82%. Interruption time: 12m."
- Incoming: "I validate health. I will follow up by throttling /generate to 70% and watch p95 for 15 minutes. Taking ownership."

Appendix B — Suggested dashboard widgets (for eng-platform dashboards)

- Operator shift summary: p50/p95 token latencies, Interruption Tax over rolling 8h, top 5 alert groups, active canaries list.
- Handoff readiness widget: kv-cache hit rate, runtime-proxy healthy replicas, rolling restart progress.

Maintenance window checklist (for scheduled work)

1) Pre-notify all affected tenants 48h prior.
2) Create ephemeral handoff channel and schedule two operators for handover overlap.
3) Confirm rollback scripts ready and smoke test them.

Document maintenance and ownership

- Author: Aisha Patel (platform-operator-experience).
- Review cadence: quarterly (next review: 2027-04-10).
- Where to change this doc: /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki (edit rights: platform-team).

Why this is different from existing guidance

This playbook formalizes the notion of Interruption Tax and prescribes a compact, time-boxed handoff script focused on minimizing needless operator work. It privileges short, reliable mitigations and explicit takeover confirmation. The heuristics unify rollout gating, alert suppression, and operator tooling into a single, executable checklist intended to reduce cognitive friction during shift boundaries.

Feedback and improvements

- Submit suggestions via PR to docs repo: git@internal:redwood/docs.git (branch: operator-handoff-improvements).
- For immediate changes to tooling snippets, open a ticket: PLATFORM-OPS-TOOLING on Jira.

End of document
